A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PbCRL study. The main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–F are readable, and retained content can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original robotic-control, autonomous-driving, and language-model experiments, together with ablations and label-noise results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds threshold-control experiments, an RLSF language-model comparison, and driving-task noise results.

M1.justification: The dead-zone loss, SNR objective, two-stage training, adaptive calibration, architectures, and policy updates are retained. Expanded explanations do not introduce a different PbCRL procedure.

E1.justification: The datasets and base tasks remain unchanged. The noisy-preference scenario expands from Goal alone in v1 Appendix F.6 to Goal and Block driving in v2 Appendix F.7, adding driving evaluation under corrupted feedback.

E2.justification: v2 Table 4 adds RLSF to the language-model comparison, which previously contained PPO, PbCRL, and Safe RLHF. RLSF's existing participation in control experiments does not make this comparison unchanged.

E3.justification: New controls test PPO-BT on Goal with training thresholds 20, 18, 15, and 10, and evaluate all six Safety Gymnasium tasks with a uniform threshold of 20. These supplement the retained protocols; the original task-specific thresholds are not replaced.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands the controls by testing whether lowering PPO-BT's threshold substitutes for PbCRL and whether uniform thresholds alter cross-task conclusions. Noise robustness also extends to driving. The dead-zone sensitivity study was already in v1 Appendix F.5; its new main-text presentation is not a new ablation.

E5.justification: Both versions state evaluation over five random seeds and retain the uncertainty information for existing results. New results use point estimates or the existing plus/minus convention; no new run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures are introduced.

E6.justification: Substantial result blocks are added for threshold controls, uniform-threshold evaluation, driving noise, and RLSF language alignment. Examples include RLSF helpfulness/harmlessness win rates of 60.4%/54.2% and PPO-BT Goal costs of 20.82 and 14.02 at training thresholds 15 and 10. Existing benchmark and ablation values are retained; different-threshold results are not same-setting performance changes.

T1.justification: The formal assumptions, dead-zone lemmas and theorems, convergence result, and Appendix B–C proofs and derivations are retained. v2 adds an explanatory roadmap and changes equation presentation and numbering without revising the mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims about distribution alignment, informative cost variation, reduced online labeling, convergence, and empirical performance. Additional supporting experiments do not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations of threshold shifting versus distribution shaping, structured driving boundaries as an explanation for noise behavior, and RLSF's mismatch with language-model sequences. Appendix F.8 also introduces helpfulness–harmlessness coupling and a Pareto-frontier interpretation, extending discussion beyond v1.

D1.justification: v2 clarifies synthetic feedback and query-budget scope for control tasks, identifies SFT as the language-model win-rate reference, and refines runtime reporting. The earlier 4–6-hour estimate becomes approximately five hours for PbCRL, split into 1.5 hours offline and 3.5 hours online, versus six hours for online baselines.

R1.justification: v2 adds Gu et al.'s 'Enhancing efficiency of safe reinforcement learning via sample manipulation' to support task-specific threshold choices and discusses RLSF's applicability to language models. Appendix A's broader research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes local language corrections, expands explanatory passages, reorganizes Appendix F, and adds an Impact Statement. The author name and publication header are updated, while the overall narrative structure is preserved.

P2.justification: v2 adds threshold-control tables, expands the language-model and noise tables, and redisplays existing dead-zone results in the main text. It also repeats the language-model table in Appendix F.8. All eight figures are retained, with localized layout and caption changes.

improvement.justification: The added threshold controls, RLSF language-model comparison, and driving noise test strengthen evaluation, while clearer feedback and runtime descriptions improve transparency. These are useful incremental gains. Some added interpretations, particularly the claim of shifting the entire language-model Pareto frontier in Appendix F.8, exceed what the reported point comparisons establish, limiting the overall improvement.
